column1: # Labeled cases for scripts/jev-triage.sh --replay, built from confirmed drift in closed target-audit issues and scripts/target-audit/signals.tsv.
# Each claim is what agnostic-ai said before the fix; each excerpt is a short quote of the vendor text that settled it.
# The says_nothing rows pair a claim with vendor text from the same target that does not address it.

column3: claim
column4: excerpt

column3: agnostic-ai writes OpenHands MCP servers to the project `config.toml` under a `[mcp]` table with `sse_servers`, `shttp_servers`, and `stdio_servers` arrays, which OpenHands reads.
column4: Current OpenHands releases don't read MCP servers from a `config.toml` `[mcp]` section (`sse_servers`, `shttp_servers`, `stdio_servers`). That format belongs to legacy OpenHands (V0).

column3: `.windsurfignore` controls which files the agent may access, a different job from `.devinignore`, and only `.codeiumignore` is a legacy name.
column4: The legacy `.windsurfignore` and `.codeiumignore` filenames are still read and enforced alongside `.devinignore`. Existing files keep working, but prefer `.devinignore` for new rules.

column3: Antigravity names no frontmatter key for rules, so a bare Markdown file in `.agents/rules/` is an always-on rule.
column4: Every `.md` file inside `rules/` must start with YAML frontmatter declaring a valid `trigger`. If a file in `.agents/rules/*.md` omits frontmatter or specifies an unrecognized `trigger` value, Antigravity silently discards the rule.

column3: Hooks have no Kilo surface yet, so hook specs skip with a warning.
column4: Drop TypeScript or JavaScript files into a `plugin/` or `plugins/` folder inside any config directory: Project: `.kilo/plugin/`. Every `.ts` or `.js` file in those directories is auto-registered at startup. `tool.execute.before` fires before a tool runs.

column3: Hook handlers written to `.claude/settings.json` keep `timeout`, `statusMessage`, `if`, and `once`, and Claude Code honors each of them there.
column4: `once`: Only honored for hooks declared in skill frontmatter; ignored in settings files and agent frontmatter

column3: `taskOutputMaxChars` in `.claude/settings.json` sets the budget for background-task output, up to 128000.
column4: Removed the deprecated TaskOutput tool; Claude reads a background task's output file with Read instead, and the `taskOutputMaxChars` setting and `TASK_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` no longer have any effect

column3: Devin has no separate write tool, so `Write` and `Edit` both map to Devin's `edit` tool in `allowed-tools` and permission rules.
column4: Custom subagent profiles and skills can grant the `write` tool using `allowed-tools`, and permission rules recognize it.

column3: A stdio server in `.cursor/mcp.json` needs no `type` field, since Cursor infers stdio from `command`.
column4: For STDIO servers (local command-line servers), configure these fields in your `mcp.json`: type, Required: Yes, Server connection type, "stdio"

column3: Cursor discovers project skills only from `.cursor/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`.
column4: For compatibility, Cursor also loads skills from Claude and Codex directories: `.claude/skills/`, `.codex/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/`, and `~/.codex/skills/`.

column3: A project syncing `claude` and `amp` has every skill loaded twice by Amp, and whether Amp dedupes across the two roots is undocumented.
column4: Amp uses the first skill with a given frontmatter name. The order is: ~/.config/agents/skills/, ~/.agents/skills/, ~/.config/amp/skills/, .agents/skills/ in the project and searched parent directories, .claude/skills/ in those directories

column3: OpenCode has no hook surface, so hook specs skip with a warning.
column4: Plugins allow you to extend OpenCode by hooking into various events and customizing behavior. `.opencode/plugins/` - Project-level plugins. Files in these directories are automatically loaded at startup.

column3: An Antigravity rule scoped to files takes `trigger: glob` frontmatter with a comma-separated `globs` string.
column4: trigger: model_decision # Required: always_on, model_decision, glob, manual. globs: "*.ts, *.tsx" # Required for glob. `globs` is "Comma-separated file glob patterns".

column3: The OpenHands CLI reads MCP servers from `~/.openhands/mcp.json`.
column4: You can also manually edit the MCP configuration file at `~/.openhands/mcp.json`.

column3: Warp reads project MCP servers from `.warp/.mcp.json`.
column4: Warp reads MCP server definitions from the following providers: Warp, `.warp/.mcp.json` at project root. Project-scoped servers from any provider require explicit approval.

column3: An Antigravity Markdown agent can list hook files in its front matter.
column4: A Markdown agent can list hook files in its front matter with a hooks: entry.

column3: Cursor reads project MCP servers from `.cursor/mcp.json`.
column4: Each rule is truncated at 30,000 characters when included in a review. The combined rules Bugbot includes for a review are capped at 100,000 characters.

column3: Windsurf reads workspace rules from `.windsurf/rules/`.
column4: Direct file edits via the `edit` and `write` tools still prompt. These tools run inside the CLI process rather than inside the sandbox, so they cannot be bounded by it.

column3: Warp reads project rules from `AGENTS.md` at the repository root.
column4: Project-scoped servers from any provider require explicit approval.

column3: Antigravity reads project skills from `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
column4: `always_on` injects the full content into the system prompt on every turn. `manual` rules load only on an @-mention.

column3: `bashOutputMaxChars` in `.claude/settings.json` caps the Bash tool's output.
column4: Removed the deprecated TaskOutput tool; Claude reads a background task's output file with Read instead
